title: improv·artist · topographic (Tara Donovan)
mutation_directive: improv artist: topographic via Tara Donovan

improv_extras.practice: millions of identical objects (cups, pins, buttons) into landscape

v1.feedback: Strong concept mapping — L-system ridges laid horizontal as geology is a genuinely clever translation of Donovan's accumulation practice, and the bone/stone/shadow palette is museum-wall restrained. The global alpha cap at 0.55 may make the terrain feel ghostly-thin rather than materially dense; consider pushing ridge-crest alpha to 0.75-0.85 so the accumulated pins read as solid mass at the peaks, tapering to transparency only in the sparse valleys. The elevated camera angle (~15 units up) risks reading as a topographic data-visualization rather than an immersive landscape — dropping camera.position.y to ~8 and nudging lookAt up slightly would put the viewer closer to ridge-line horizon and strengthen the geological presence.

v2.feedback: Strong concept mapping — L-system as ridge skeleton with pin accumulation is faithful Donovan logic. The terrain should read within 2s at the oblique camera angle, but consider adding subtle distance-based alpha fade or soft fog to enhance the vast-in-miniature quality and separate foreground crests from background valleys. Pin height contrast between ridge crests and valley floors could be more pronounced (currently 0.08–0.30 range is subtle at this scale) to strengthen the silhouette when viewed from the side. A single very slow downward camera drift over 60s would add a satellite-descent reveal without violating the still-camera preference.
v2.raw:

**Concept fidelity**: L-system branching reinterpreted as horizontal ridge lines with 70k pin-like vertical particles accumulating along them is a genuinely clever mapping of Donovan's practice (millions of identical objects → landscape).
